dimensions.assessment: Affects offshore oil and gas operators, applicants, state reef programs, and fishers utilizing covered waters.
dimensions.evidence: An Applicant may elect to Reef in Place the Inactive Structure

dimensions.assessment: Changes decommissioning and liability obligations for energy operators and transfers long-term maintenance and liability to states.
dimensions.evidence: the State shall be ... exclusively responsible and liable for the Approved structure

dimensions.assessment: States may receive funds not exceeding 50 percent of the cost savings gained by the applicant due to reefing.
dimensions.evidence: does not exceed 50 percent of the cost savings gained by the Applicant due to reefing

dimensions.assessment: Amends the National Fishing Enhancement Act of 1984 and the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to establish new regulatory procedures and restrictions on removal orders.
dimensions.evidence: The National Fishing Enhancement Act of 1984 (33 U.S.C. 2101 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Provides ongoing procedures and permanent structural changes in how offshore structures are decommissioned in covered waters.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this Act shall eliminate, modify or otherwise limit the ability of any party from pursuing the reefing

missing_information: Exact number of structures or total financial savings expected across the industry
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a formal statutory process for turning inactive offshore oil and gas platforms and pipelines into artificial reefs, impacting offshore energy operators, state reef programs, and commercial and recreational fishers.
